summary: Modern databases and data platforms have rapidly embedded AI/ML capabilities directly into the engine, driven by the rise of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and the fact that an estimated 75% of enterprise AI applications will depend on vector search by 2026. Vector database adoption grew 377% year over year — the fastest among LLM-related technologies — pushing platforms to offer native vector indexing, in-database LLM inference, and semantic search alongside traditional analytics. The dominant pattern is to keep operational data, embeddings, and governance together to reduce data silos and complex pipelines.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless access to hosted LLMs (via COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, EXTRACT_ANSWER functions), plus Cortex Search for semantic/hybrid retrieval and Cortex Analyst for natural-language querying. Snowflake Postgres now unifies the popular open-source database with analytics and AI on a single governed platform, and the Horizon Catalog adds governance over AI-ready data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in. Snowflake supports a VECTOR data type and vector similarity functions (VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY, etc.), and Cortex Search offers managed semantic/hybrid retrieval natively within the platform.
databases.llm_integration: First-party hosted LLMs (including Anthropic Claude, Mistral, Meta Llama, Snowflake Arctic) accessed directly through SQL Cortex functions; no external API wiring required.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based pricing in Snowflake credits; Cortex LLM functions are billed per token/compute, and vector/search serverless features consume credits. No separate licensing for Cortex beyond compute usage.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI integration (Gemini), vector search, and BigQuery Graph
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create and run ML models (regression, classification, forecasting, clustering) using SQL, and integrates with Vertex AI for generative AI and remote model inference (e.g., Gemini). It supports embeddings generation, vector/text/hybrid search for RAG applications, and BigQuery Graph for relationship analysis.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in. BigQuery supports the VECTOR_SEARCH function and CREATE VECTOR INDEX for storing and querying embeddings directly, plus hybrid (vector + keyword) search.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI and Gemini models via remote models and ML.GENERATE_TEXT / ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING functions callable from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Pay-per-query (on-demand bytes scanned) or capacity-based slots; ML inference and Vertex AI model calls incur additional charges based on the underlying model/compute.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector extension for vector storage/search and pgai for in-database LLM/embedding workflows
databases.description: Core PostgreSQL has no built-in AI, but the pgvector extension adds a vector column type with similarity operators and ANN indexes (HNSW, IVFFlat), and pgai (from Timescale) adds functions to generate embeddings and call LLMs directly from SQL. Together they turn Postgres into a capable RAG backend while keeping relational and vector data together.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to core PostgreSQL. Vector search is provided only via the third-party pgvector extension; it is widely used and robust but is an add-on, not a built-in engine capability.
databases.llm_integration: Via pgai and similar extensions, which can call external providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Ollama) to generate embeddings and completions from SQL; also wired into application code or frameworks like LangChain.
databases.pricing_notes: Open-source and free; extensions are free. Costs depend on hosting (self-managed, or managed services such as Timescale, Supabase, Neon, RDS) plus any external LLM API usage.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning (SQL-based integration with Amazon SageMaker, Bedrock, and Comprehend)
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you invoke ML models from SQL queries, passing row data to Amazon SageMaker, Amazon Bedrock (for generative AI), or Amazon Comprehend (for sentiment/NLP) and returning predictions as part of the query result, enabling inference on transactional data without moving it.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to Aurora ML itself. Vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL is available only through the pgvector extension, which is a third-party add-on rather than a built-in Aurora ML feature.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock foundation models (e.g., Claude, Titan) and SageMaker-hosted models through SQL functions for in-database inference and embeddings.
databases.pricing_notes: No extra charge for the Aurora ML feature itself; you pay standard Aurora instance/storage costs plus the underlying SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend usage charges.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML (SQL-based model creation and inference via Amazon SageMaker and Bedrock)
databases.description: Redshift ML allows analysts to create, train, and deploy ML models using standard SQL (CREATE MODEL), automatically leveraging Amazon SageMaker Autopilot behind the scenes, and to run predictions directly in the data warehouse. It also supports generative AI through integration with Amazon Bedrock for LLM functions.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not natively built into Redshift ML. Redshift has introduced vector/embedding capabilities and Bedrock-based embedding generation, but dedicated native vector similarity search is limited; for production vector search AWS typically points to OpenSearch or pgvector on Aurora/RDS.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock for LLM-based generation and embeddings via SQL functions, and with SageMaker for custom models.
databases.pricing_notes: No separate charge for the Redshift ML feature; costs come from Redshift compute/storage plus SageMaker training and Bedrock inference usage.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, agents) with Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Mosaic AI provides end-to-end GenAI tooling — foundation model fine-tuning, model serving, AI agents, and evaluation — on the Lakehouse, while Databricks Vector Search provides a managed, serverless vector index synced to Delta tables for RAG. Governance is unified through Unity Catalog.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in. Databricks Vector Search is a first-party managed vector database that automatically keeps embeddings in sync with source Delta tables and supports similarity and hybrid search.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Model Serving hosts open and proprietary foundation models (Llama, DBRX, and external providers like OpenAI/Anthropic) with Foundation Model APIs callable from notebooks and SQL/AI functions.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks DBUs; Vector Search and Model Serving are billed by provisioned/serverless compute and token throughput, on top of underlying cloud infrastructure.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search for semantic retrieval and RAG on operational documents
databases.description: Atlas Vector Search lets you store embeddings alongside JSON documents and run approximate nearest-neighbor similarity queries natively in the Atlas aggregation pipeline, enabling semantic search and RAG without a separate vector store. It supports combining vector, full-text, and metadata filtering for hybrid search.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in (within MongoDB Atlas). Vector Search is a first-class Atlas feature using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage and dedicated vector indexes; note it is an Atlas (managed cloud) capability rather than part of self-hosted community MongoDB.
databases.llm_integration: No hosted LLMs of its own; integrates with external embedding/LLM providers (OpenAI, Cohere, Hugging Face, Azure OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock) and frameworks like LangChain/LlamaIndex for embedding generation and RAG.
databases.pricing_notes: Included with Atlas; vector search runs on dedicated Search Nodes or shared cluster resources, so cost scales with cluster tier and Search Node provisioning. External embedding/LLM API costs are separate.
